unit.title: Concession, cause, purpose & result
unit.subtitle: aunque, porque, para que, así que — and the mood each one demands

grammar.title: Link your ideas with precision
grammar.intro: Sophisticated Spanish connects clauses: concession (aunque), cause (porque, como), purpose (para que) and result (así que, tan… que). The tricky part is mood: aunque + indicative states a real fact, but aunque + subjunctive concedes a hypothesis. Purpose clauses always take the subjunctive. Master these four connectors and your Spanish gains real nuance.

sections.heading: Concession: aunque + indicative vs subjunctive
sections.body: Aunque + indicative = a real, known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = a hypothesis or a concession “even if”. Also: a pesar de que, por más que:

ex.en: Even though it's raining, I'm going out.
Even if it rains, I'll go out.

sections.heading: Cause: porque, ya que, como, puesto que
sections.body: Porque answers “why”. Como states a cause and goes at the start of the sentence. Ya que / puesto que / debido a que introduce a known reason:

ex.en: Since I arrived late, I missed the train.
I didn't go because I was ill.

sections.heading: Purpose: para que + subjunctive / para + inf
sections.body: Same subject → para + infinitive. Different subject → para que + subjunctive. Also a fin de que + subjunctive:

ex.en: I'm explaining it so that you understand it.
I study (in order) to pass the exam.

sections.heading: Result: así que, de modo que, tan/tanto… que
sections.body: Así que / de modo que = “so”. Tan + adjective/adverb + que; tanto/-a/-os/-as + noun + que, or verb + tanto que. De ahí que takes the subjunctive:

ex.en: I was so tired that I fell asleep.

ex.es: Habló tanto que se quedó sin voz.
ex.en: He talked so much that he lost his voice.

takeaways: aunque + indicative = real fact (Aunque llueve, salgo); aunque + subjunctive = hypothesis (Aunque llueva, saldré).
Cause: porque, ya que, puesto que, debido a que; como goes sentence-initial.
Purpose: para + infinitive (same subject), para que + subjunctive (different subject).
Result: así que, de modo que; tan + adj/adv + que, tanto + noun/verb + que; de ahí que + subjunctive.

mistakes.why: A future hypothesis takes the subjunctive: aunque llueva.

mistakes.w: Estaba tanto cansado que me dormí.
mistakes.r: Estaba tan cansado que me dormí.
mistakes.why: Before an adjective use tan, not tanto: tan cansado.

mistakes.w: Te lo explico para que lo entiendes.
mistakes.r: Te lo explico para que lo entiendas.
mistakes.why: para que always takes the subjunctive: entiendas.

exercises.prompt_en: Even if it rains tomorrow, I'll go anyway.
exercises.no: Concession “even if” uses aunque + subjunctive: “Aunque llueva…”.

exercises.prompt: Te lo digo para que lo ___ (different subject).
exercises.prompt_en: I'm telling you so that you understand it.
exercises.no: para que always takes the subjunctive: “para que lo entiendas”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “I was so tired that I fell asleep.”
exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! tan + adjetivo + que: tan cansado que.
exercises.no: Before an adjective use tan: “Estaba tan cansado que me dormí”.

exercises.prompt_en: Since I arrived late, I missed the train.
exercises.hint: A cause connector that goes at the start of the sentence.
exercises.ok: ¡Bien! como = causa, al inicio de la frase.
exercises.no: A sentence-initial cause uses como: “Como llegué tarde, perdí el tren”.

exercises.prompt: Match each connector to its function.
exercises.ok: ¡Excelente! Concesión, causa, finalidad y consecuencia, claras.

exercises.tts: Habló tanto que se quedó sin voz.
accepted: hablo tanto que se quedo sin voz
exercises.translation: He talked so much that he lost his voice.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Habló tanto que se quedó sin voz.”
exercises.no: It was: “Habló tanto que se quedó sin voz.” (verb + tanto que).

exercises.scenario: Deciding whether to go to the beach despite the forecast 🌦️

lines.speaker: Sofía
lines.es: Dicen que quizá llueva esta tarde. ¿Vamos a la playa igualmente?
lines.en: They say it might rain this afternoon. Shall we go to the beach anyway?

exercises.no: For an uncertain future, use aunque + subjunctive: “aunque llueva, vamos”.

exercises.say: Aunque llueva, saldré, así que no te preocupes
exercises.en: Even if it rains, I'll go out, so don't worry
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “aunque llueva… así que”.
